mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate financing costs decrease.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.1% over the prior 3 months, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, triggering immediate equity sell-offs as recession risks rise, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE rises by >0.3pp in a month, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in housing starts and retail sales exceeding 0.5% in the same month indicate broad-based consumer demand weakness, causing short-term equity sell-offs as corporate revenue growth prospects deteriorate, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS decline >0.5% in same month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS decline by >0.5% in the same month, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In strong industrial growth regimes (INDPRO > 110), a monthly decline in industrial production signals supply chain disruption and economic slowdown, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate output expectations fall.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO > 110 and INDPRO declines by >0.5% in a month, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts signals strengthening consumer demand and economic activity, supporting corporate earnings growth and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as residential investment expands.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where HOUST increases by at least 0.5% over the prior 3 months, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI index increase exceeding 0.3% signals accelerating inflation, prompting expectations of tighter monetary policy that reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL rises by >0.3% in a month, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent decline in payroll growth (PAYEMS) by >0.2% and unemployment rate increase (UNRATE) by >0.2pp signals severe labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and corporate profits, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS declines >0.2% and UNRATE rises >0.2pp in same month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where PAYEMS declines by >0.2% and UNRATE rises by >0.2pp in the same month, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high housing demand regimes (HOUST > 1800), a monthly decline in housing starts signals cooling real estate activity, reducing consumer confidence and corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where HOUST > 1800 and HOUST declines by >0.5% in a month, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.
